change: Optional Agent Monitor HTTP backend for the standalone OpenCode V2 plugin, preserving native forms and per-call refusals for the default stub.

packaged_live_tests.note: Current 0.3.0 bundle was tested directly; prior packaged checks are recorded separately under historical_validation.

verified: Native forms bind immutable request ID, phase, session, digest and fields; only explicit allow releases one checkpoint.
Desktop renderer requires metadata.kind=question and reads field.title; native forms provide both.
Installed Desktop 2.0.22 and exact TUI 2.0.22 render these field types and serialize string option values to the exact decision object.
Default connection discovers only its own existing service and checks server PID and version.
Classifier unavailability stays fail-open; native form failure cancels only the current checkpoint.
Post replacement scrubs the entire result/error; rejection never latches a session.
Monitor requests bind the registered run, session, tool call, exact arguments and policy version; native forms cannot override a monitor decision.
A hard monitor BLOCK rejects one call. Transport, integrity and incomplete execution failures poison the run and prevent later model/tool hooks.
Final argument and cancellation checks run after awaited start/result and audit operations.
Expired or invalidated pending approvals fail instead of polling indefinitely.

limits: The default classifier remains an always-deny stub and its unavailability intentionally fails open. The optional monitor backend fails closed.
No rollback after post, OS sandbox, or provider-hosted tool enforcement.
Live MCP uses direct tools with codemode=false; unit tests cover CodeMode IDs and parallel/child calls.
Pre refusals may have no post hook because the tool did not execute.
Already-running parallel tools may finish; each intercepted checkpoint requires its own decision.
An independently installed legacy V1 adapter can still latch sessions; remove it from discovery when upgrading.
Self-load failures before hook registration cannot be enforced by the plugin.
Feedback is returned through tool error/result and asks the model to explain it. No separate assistant message is inserted; exact final chat wording is not guaranteed.
Tool names and classifier reasons are limited to 200 and 1000 source characters, with an explicit truncation marker.
Desktop/TUI UI compatibility verified from installed renderer code; no manual visual click test.
Noninteractive opencode run cancels forms; interactive TUI is required for manual approvals.
V1 1.18.11 retains its browser confirmation UI; native forms are V2-only.
If a form create request loses its acknowledgement and commits after cleanup, an inert pending card can remain; it cannot release the cancelled action.
Monitor mode requires private service credentials outside the workspace, the same real workspace, a single session, and registered tool names; explicit toolMap entries map verified MCP names.
Monitor mode rejects unmediated shell commands, child sessions, context attachments and CodeMode calls. It does not provide an OS sandbox.
Post reporting records completion/error and does not represent a safety verdict or rollback.

live_tests.model: local deterministic OpenAI-compatible fixture; no external LLM
live_tests.interaction: session.create/prompt/wait and native form list/get/reply/cancel HTTP APIs; visual UI clicks not tested
verification: Each native form is visible to the Desktop selector (kind=question), has a quarantine field title and explicit allow/reject choices without a default.
Pre gates prevent file effects while pending or rejected. Post gates prevent result/error data reaching the next model request until allowed.
After reject/cancel the same session executes an independently approved tool and completes a later user turn.
No browser opener is launched and no separate sensor approval server control file is created, even with legacy openBrowser=true.
Managed OpenCode service is discovered automatically without serverURL; credentials come from its registration, and PID/version checks pass.
Text-only, disabled and startup-failure behavior remains compatible with session continuation.

packaged_live_tests.installation: Standalone packaged bundle without plugin node_modules
packaged_live_tests.interaction: Native session/form APIs; no visual UI click automation
verification: Native session forms show bound tool, phase, classifier reason and explicit choices.
Reject blocks the specific operation/result and permits another tool and next turn in the same session.
Managed service discovery works without explicit serverURL.
No external browser opener or separate sensor control.json was used.

monitor_live_tests.runtime: actual pinned OpenCode 2.0.22 with the Python Agent Monitor service
monitor_live_tests.model: local deterministic OpenAI-compatible fixture; no external LLM
monitor_live_tests.interaction: Trusted administrator HTTP fixture approves or rejects the exact pending action; no native UI approval or CLI subprocess test.
verification: Allowed actions acquire a single-use start permit before tool execution and report completion.
Policy BLOCK prevents the file effect; exact monitor approval permits it and rejection prevents it.
Sensitive reads taint the registered run before execution and record their result.
Unavailable monitor prevents the first model request and tool execution.
